status.description: Doctor verdict for a harness: ok (usable), degraded (usable with limitations), or unavailable.

id.description: Harness id (codex, claude, cursor, opencode, raw-api, ...).

display_name.description: Human display name of the harness.

kind.description: Kind of harness adapter: a local vendor CLI, a remote API, or a fake used for tests.

adapter_version.description: Version of the Claudexor adapter itself.

provider_family.description: Vendor/provider family a harness routes to, used for route-diversity reasoning; open-ended via "unknown".

items.description: Concrete credential source used or probed by a harness.

preferred_source.description: Auth source the adapter prefers; null when it has no preference.

kind.description: Mechanism that carries a credential to the harness process (config file, env var, OAuth token env, OS keychain, HTTP header, or none).

items.description: Which relocation lever moves the credential into a scoped environment (HOME, a config dir override, env injection, or none).

relocatable_by.description: Relocation levers that can move this transport into a scoped environment.

items.description: Host platform used to resolve credential and managed-login policy.

platforms.description: Host platforms on which this physical credential transport applies; absent means every supported platform for backward compatibility.

items.description: How a credential from one auth source physically reaches the harness process.

credential_transports.description: Declared credential transports per auth source.

platforms.description: Nonempty host-platform set governed by this policy row.

identity_scope.description: Identity boundary selected by a credential profile: the named profile itself or the host OS user/login vault.

max_enabled_profiles.description: Maximum enabled profile bindings on these platforms; null means unbounded.

cleanup_owner.description: Who owns cleanup of the credential when its Claudexor profile binding is removed.

items.description: Platform-specific identity scope, enabled-profile cardinality, and credential cleanup ownership for one auth source.

credential_profile_policies.description: Platform-specific profile identity/cardinality/cleanup policy; absent uses the backward-compatible profile-scoped, unbounded, Claudexor-owned defaults.

stdin.description: Input transport the vendor login command requires.

anyOf.description: Managed-login input requirement; command, argv, flow, and time window remain owned by the native-login registry.

managed_login.description: Managed subscription-login input requirement; null means this harness defines no managed login, absent is a legacy manifest.

auth.description: Declared auth routing facts for a harness.

readonly_mechanism.description: How a harness applies read-only access: a filesystem sandbox, permission denial, a tool allowlist, or none (read-only intent is advisory).

write_mechanism.description: How workspace_write access is CONFINED for a harness: a filesystem/network base sandbox (codex seatbelt; the harness's native automatic reviewer may still admit individual actions outside it, so fs_sandbox does not mean every admitted action stays inside), a tool-permission policy with no FS/network fence (claude — an allowed shell is unconfined), or none (write intent is advisory).

auxiliary_writable_roots.description: The adapter applies HarnessRunSpec.auxiliary_writable_roots natively under workspace_write, and a later spec carrying none receives no earlier grant; false = such a lane refuses (explicit pool) or is filtered (auto pool).

access_control.description: Declared access-control facts for a harness.

items.description: Isolation containment level an adapter supports for run environments, from env/file injection through scoped-HOME keychain bridging or a private per-profile keychain to process sandboxes and containers.

supported_containment.description: Containment mechanisms the adapter can run under.

isolation.description: Declared isolation containment facts for a harness.

kind.description: Kind of attached resource: image input or generic file bytes.

transport.description: Native adapter transport used for one supported attachment class.

items.description: Finite MIME, size, count and transport limits declared by one adapter.

scope.description: All text input items in one native turn; separate instructions are excluded.

verified_against.description: Native runtime version against which the bound was observed.

items.description: Adapter-owned observed input bound, not a predictive refusal or a model-window claim.

mcp_injection.description: The adapter can inject engine-owned MCP servers into the harness sandbox (browser tool, delegation belt); false = browser MCP is refused and Delegate degrades to ordinary Agent with a durable typed receipt.

mcp_injection_requires_full_access.description: An injected MCP server can only reach the daemon (belt) at full access; below it the harness sandbox cancels the call. true => Delegate below full access degrades to ordinary Agent with a durable typed receipt.

live_input.description: How a live message enters a running session: mid_turn (consumed inside the active turn), next_tool_boundary (queued until the same turn's next tool boundary), none (no truthful channel; the engine answers unsupported).

items.description: Native prompt-cache lifetime for the main conversation and helper requests of a harness that declares it. Omission sends no override: native defaults, profile settings and the inherited environment stay in effect.

prompt_cache_ttls.description: Prompt-cache lifetimes this adapter translates into native controls; a requested lifetime outside the list (or with the list absent) is disclosed as ignored.

capability_profile.description: Structured per-harness facts the engine consumes: auth routing, isolation containment, readonly mechanism, finite attachment inputs, MCP injection, live input into a running session, and translated prompt-cache lifetimes.

items.description: Advisory service preference. Fast or Economy may use ordinary Standard service; fallback never introduces Fast. Omission preserves native defaults. Explicit native serviceTier takes precedence.

processing_preferences.description: Service preferences translated by this adapter; model/account support is separate.

plan.description: The harness can produce plans (plan intent).

implement.description: The harness can implement code changes (implement intent).

implementation_transport.description: Typed producer/consumer transport used when implement=true.

create_from_scratch.description: The harness can scaffold new projects (create_from_scratch intent).

review.description: The harness can act as a reviewer (review intent).

verify.description: The harness can act as the FinalVerifier (verify intent).

synthesize.description: The harness can synthesize across candidate outputs (synthesize intent).

read_files.description: The harness can read project files.

browser_tool.description: The adapter can inject a browser-automation MCP server (Playwright MCP) the harness drives as browser_* tools; never injected when web policy is off.

web_policy.description: How a harness can honor the external web policy: native (a native config surface), tools (permissioned tools the adapter can allow/deny), uncontrolled (can reach the web but exposes no enforceable switch), or none (no web access at all).

tool_lists.description: Honors tool_permission_policy allow/deny lists (e.g. a native --allowedTools flag).

interactive.description: The adapter can surface interactive user questions (interaction_requested events) and deliver typed answers back into the live session.

json_schema_output.description: The harness can constrain its final message to a caller-supplied JSON Schema (native structured-output flag).

work_report_transport.description: How the harness carries the D-16 WorkReport envelope: constrained (native schema transport), validated (instructed terminal metadata), or unsupported (work_state stays unverified).

structured_output_channel.description: Where a schema-constrained answer surfaces: side_tool (rides a tool; final message stays markdown) or final_message (constrains the final message itself).

items.description: Cross-harness reasoning-effort level as a lowercase slug (open vocabulary, mirroring the vendor contract); adapters advertise the levels they accept per model, ordered weakest to strongest by the vendor itself, and a shared normalizer passes advertised levels through, clamps inside the vendor order, places a word the vendor order lacks by the shared preference order (none < minimal < low < medium < high < xhigh < max < ultra) onto an advertised level, and refuses words neither order places.

effort_levels.description: Ordered (weakest to strongest) reasoning-effort levels this harness accepts across all its models; empty means effort is not a tunable surface.

levels.description: Ordered (weakest to strongest) reasoning-effort levels this model advertises, in the vendor's own order.

default.description: The effort level the vendor uses for this model when none is requested.

additionalProperties.description: Reasoning-effort vocabulary a single model advertises.

model_effort_levels.description: Per-model advertised reasoning-effort vocabulary keyed by model id; a model absent here falls back to the harness-wide effort_levels union.

effort_levels_verified_against.description: Vendor CLI version the effort ladders were last verified against; null = never verified / not applicable.

model_inventory_routes.description: Credential routes supported by the adapter's live models() producer; omitted preserves all-route support. Other routes use manifest known_models, never another account's live inventory.

model_inventory_absence.description: Whether an absence from this harness's model lists (the live models() answer and the manifest known_models alike) proves a model is ABSENT; omitted = authoritative (an unlisted model is refused). advisory = absence is not proof, so an explicit model is forwarded to the vendor and disclosed instead of refused.

billing.description: base = billed like the listed row; service_tier = the provider may serve it on another service tier billed at that tier's rate.

items.description: One declared request-time routing suffix and its billing effect.

model_routing_variants.description: Request-time routing suffixes this harness's provider accepts on a listed model id; an id ending in declared suffixes is admitted when the id without them is an exact catalog row. Omitted = exact catalog membership only.

reason.description: provider_web_search = the provider would search the web for the request, outside this route's web policy.

items.description: One declared request-time suffix this harness refuses, and why.

model_refused_variants.description: Request-time suffixes this harness refuses in any position after the base id, whether or not a catalog lists the id or could be read. Omitted = none.

routes.description: Credential routes this model is available on.

known_models.description: Manifest-declared model ids/aliases this harness accepts (bare string = every credential route; object form scopes a model to specific routes), used as the model truth source when the adapter has no live inventory and judged under model_inventory_absence: an authoritative harness refuses an explicit model outside it, an advisory harness forwards it with a note.

known_models_verified_against.description: Vendor CLI version the known_models hints were last verified against; null = never verified / not applicable.

capabilities.description: Declared harness capabilities the engine actually consumes for intent gating, routing, knob support, and disclosure.

auth_modes.description: Auth modes the harness supports (availability only, not readiness).

items.description: Active filesystem/command access profile for a run: readonly (no writes), workspace_write (use the harness's native workspace-write policy), full (unrestricted; requires the per-repo trust allow for a run an operator starts at a surface, not for an execution.delegated run), inherit_native (defer to the harness's own native settings).

access_profiles_supported.description: Access profiles the adapter can translate to its harness.

anyOf.description: Static manifest an adapter declares for its harness: identity, kind, capabilities, auth modes, and access profiles.

manifest.description: The harness's declared manifest, when available.

enabledIntents.description: Intents an explicit selection of this harness may run: capability intents its doctor enables. A degraded harness keeps the intents its doctor still enables, with its reasons; an unavailable harness has none.

routableIntents.description: Intents the automatic (Auto pool) routing may choose this harness for: enabledIntents while the doctor reports ok, empty for a degraded or unavailable harness. Explicit selection reads enabledIntents instead.

status.description: Outcome of the check: pass, fail, or skip.

duration_ms.description: How long the check took, in milliseconds.

items.description: Result of a conformance probe for one capability check.
Doctor-backed readiness for one exact credential source.

authSources.description: Doctor-backed readiness by authentication source; an empty array means readiness was not reported.

id.description: Stable machine id of the check (adapter probe id or auth source).

kind.description: What KIND of readiness this is: binary presence, credential source, isolated smoke, configured-model validity, or a generic capability probe.

title.description: Human display name of the check.

status.description: Outcome; skip = not run / not applicable.

detail.description: Redacted human-readable evidence for the outcome.

readiness.description: Display-ready readiness checks, daemon-normalized from the raw evidence.

configuredModel.description: The user's configured per-harness default model, if any.

status.description: Whether the configured model is admitted (listed, or unlisted on an advisory harness) or refused by an authoritative list.

configuredModelCheck.description: Truth-source check of configuredModel under the harness's own absence declaration; ok with a message is an advisory admission; null when no model is configured.

available.description: Whether this harness can receive the packaged delegation belt.

reason.description: Stable reason for the current delegation capability verdict.

remediation.description: Concrete update/repair guidance when unavailable; null when ready.

requiresFullAccess.description: Whether this harness can reach the belt only under a full-access profile.

anyOf.description: Engine-owned Delegate capability projection for one harness and installed runtime.

delegation.description: Engine-owned Delegate capability for this harness and installed runtime; null on legacy status rows.

mode.description: in_app requests the daemon-hosted login flow; external_terminal requests the existing client PTY flow.

anyOf.description: Effective setup-login flow for this harness on the current host.

setupLogin.description: Effective setup-login flow for this harness on the current host; current producers emit null or an object, while omission identifies a legacy row.

items.description: Doctor-backed status row for one harness: status, intents, checks, and configured-model validity.

harnesses.description: Status rows for all known harnesses.

git.description: Execution-location Git readiness; omitted by daemons predating capability projection.
